title: Stress-testing 7,000 simultaneous enemies in my browser roguelike — built with Claude Code as a pair-programmer
author: CrisosDev
selftext:
Raw gameplay clip below is a built-in stress-test mode for *Just Dying*, running in the browser build (React 19 + PixiJS 8). It ramps enemy count through fixed steps — 300 → 600 → 1,191 → 1,994 → 2,996 → 4,466 → 7,011 — to find where the frame budget breaks.

Where generative AI actually came in: I've been using Claude Code as an active collaborator on the engine itself, not just autocomplete. A few concrete examples from building this exact tool:

* Iterating live on a spatial-hash collision system and a custom PixiJS particle pipeline, with Claude reading the render loop and flagging where a per-frame allocation was killing GC.
* Debugging a shader precision bug where the enemy grid flickered at large world coordinates (float32 hash collisions) — Claude traced it to the hash function, not the grid logic, which wasn't where I was looking.
* Designing the stress-test's spawn pacing: originally the enemy counter was tied to real alive-enemy counts, which stalled under a strong AoE loadout because kills outpaced spawns. We iterated through a few approaches together before landing on decoupling the *displayed* counter from the actual entity count — it now ramps and holds on schedule regardless of what the AoE is doing to the horde.

Happy to go deeper on any of the systems (spatial hashing, the render/ECS split, worker-based combat sim) if people want specifics.

You can try the game yourself — playable demo on [itch.io](https://justdying.itch.io/just-dying) (browser, same build this stress-test runs on) and on [Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4656170/Just_Dying_Demo/).
